name: MMAU
intro: MMAU 是一个面向音频语言模型的大规模多任务音频理解与推理 benchmark。论文 v1 的最终集包含 10,000 道覆盖语音、环境声和音乐的专家标注多选题；27 类任务中有 11 类信息抽取任务和 16 类推理任务。
build_method: 七步专家策展, 专家标注与过滤, GPT-4选项增强, 专家复核
task_type: 音频理解, 音频推理
eval_feature: 五次选项乱序多数票, 稳健正则与字符串匹配, 多提示取最佳, 27类任务
openness_en: Partly Public (Apache-2.0 repository; no license metadata on the pinned HF mirror; source-audio rights vary; main-test gold is withheld)
build_method_en: Seven-step Expert Curation, Expert Annotation and Filtering, GPT-4 Option Augmentation, Expert Review
eval_feature_en: Five option-order shuffles with majority vote, Robust regex and string matching, Best across prompt sets, 27 tasks
intro_en: MMAU is a massive multi-task audio understanding and reasoning benchmark for audio-language models. Paper v1 finalizes 10,000 expert-annotated multiple-choice questions over speech, environmental sounds, and music; its 27 tasks comprise 11 information-extraction tasks and 16 reasoning tasks.

drawio_review_note: Reviewed against the sole arXiv version, arXiv:2410.19168v1 (submitted 2024-10-24; reviewed PDF SHA-256 455dbfa3f7cb020120e3e0d0c624f707324e9596dd3b26b8c82e9b855580d41a), especially Sections 3.1-3.2 and 4, Tables 1 and 6, and Appendices C, E, and L; the public lmms-lab/mmau Hugging Face mirror pinned at bd09999670e77f5452c23a09435ee437bd0e1406 (2025-03-17); the official Sakshi113/MMAU repository pinned at 110127f54c0dfba3faa5ec9feee4a7e4148679c5, whose evaluation.py last changed at 74682927cf7f434cc9ed585b1f8a5e6150381e91; the current official HF Space scorer pinned at 70339a493a44c7db3d847e07fc8fc2b1f1adb9f8; the arXiv-linked homepage source pinned at b6ad5cf8157a0d959d6de579367b15fc9a257220; and the legacy mmaubench.github.io page source pinned at 1dd48dfc55637b7616b7263ed7a3210de9d01f04. Paper v1 defines exactly seven named construction stages: Source Selection; Task Curation; Expert Annotation; Expert Filtering; Option Augmentation; Expert Review; and MMAU Finalization. Table 6 lists 13 final source categories whose counts sum to 10,000: AudioSet 2,788; AudioSet Strong 391; MUStARD 405; MELD 540; VoxCeleb-1 633; IEMOCAP 515; MusicBench 1,937; MTG-Jamendo 32; SDD 277; MusicCaps 514; GuitarSet 506; MUSDB18 68; and Synthetic 1,394. Source selection prioritizes real recordings. Domain experts reduce 90 candidate tasks to 27 real-world-feasible tasks; experts and authors iteratively select plausible clips and author English MCQ questions and gold answers requiring complex reasoning and domain knowledge. The guidelines require complete listening, one non-corrupt audio, task/difficulty/dataset tags, and no audio-name leakage. The main text calls filtering a separate expert team, but Appendix C says the same three-person annotation-and-filtering pool filters the samples; a second three-person pool handles Expert Review, with one expert per domain in each pool. The annotation/filtering pool checks the benchmark twice. The counts are approximate, not an exact subtraction contract: approximately 11,000 annotated pairs, approximately 800 removed in filtering, and approximately 200 removed in review, followed by exactly 10,000 selected final questions. GPT-4 option augmentation contains another paper-internal tension: Section 3.2 says distractors are based on audio and question context, while the Appendix-L prompt actually supplies question type, question, and correct answer with no audio input. That prompt requests six contrastive options plus the correct answer using ten named distractor patterns, limits each option to 50 words, and emits JSON; the paper does not disclose how those candidates are reduced to the released choice sets. Expert Review rechecks answers and augmented options and tags task and required skills. Finalization balances all 27 task types and equal domain coverage, then selects 1,000 test-mini and 9,000 main-test questions. Paper v1 reports 11 information-extraction tasks with 3,499 questions and 16 reasoning tasks with 6,501 questions, task-domain counts of speech 10, music 10, and sound 7, and easy/medium/hard proportions of 22/56/22. Both the current arXiv-linked project page and the legacy page instead say 12 information-retrieval and 15 reasoning task types; the legacy page also retains a broken GitHub URL containing YOUR REPO HERE. The diagram follows paper v1 and preserves the page conflict. The pinned HF mirror is public and ungated, contains 70 test plus eight test_mini Parquet shards, and declares 9,000 plus 1,000 examples, 14,540,107,176 downloaded bytes, and 15,423,652,641 dataset bytes. Its 11 fields are id, audio at 192 kHz, question, choices as a JSON-encoded string, answer, dataset, task, split, category, sub-category, and difficulty; the viewer exposes test gold as the NA sentinel while test-mini has answers. This differs from the later official JSON files, which use audio_id paths and array-valued choices. The pinned HF mirror predates the untagged MMAU-v05.15.25 update; the official README says that update revised approximately 25% of questions/answers and 5% of audio, but does not map the named version to an immutable HF revision. Paper evaluation uses micro-averaged accuracy: try multiple prompt sets, ask for one option, shuffle option order five times, parse open responses with robust regular expressions and response-processing workflows, string-match to a provided option, take the most frequent option across the five orders, and report the best prompt result. Exact prompt-set texts/count, decoding and stop settings, shuffle seed/order schedule, vote-tie rule, and paper-time parser implementation are not released. The current HF Space does not run that inference protocol; it joins submitted ids to a private ground-truth dataset fetched without a revision pin, accepts model_prediction, tokenizes list predictions by joining and other values through str(), lowercases regex word tokens, requires every gold token, and rejects tokens unique to incorrect options while ignoring order and multiplicity and allowing unrelated tokens. Missing or unknown ids are skipped. A submitted row whose id overlaps ground truth enters the denominator even when its prediction is missing, null, or empty and is counted wrong; completely omitted ground-truth ids do not enter the denominator. Duplicate submitted ids are counted repeatedly, no 9,000-id completeness check exists, and zero overlap returns an error. The older repository evaluation.py is a different and defective local contract: it expects model_output although the README says model_prediction, skips missing-key rows so no_pred_count is unreachable, divides by zero when every row is skipped, and assumes list-valued choices although the pinned HF mirror stores a string. Openness is therefore conservative: the repository added an Apache-2.0 LICENSE in July 2025, the pinned HF card declares no license metadata, the paper requires compliance with each source's copyright/license, main-test gold remains private, and neither the construction code nor a version-pinned private ground-truth snapshot is public. Formal publication evidence [site-a11m-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2519×1401 (English) and 2515×1401 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2517×1399 and 2513×1399. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
